posts.title: Parfums Dusita Mocha Absolu fragrance review
posts.description: The French brand Parfums Dusita lately reinvents gourmand accords in an ineffable way, beyond merely comforting; chic, refined, never inducing the diabetic coma so many other brands are prone to –and with that, Giardini di Toscana I'm looking at you... posts.title: Omonde Jayne Vanille Aube fragrance review
posts.description: Vanilla Aube by Ormonde Jayne is lovely: All the colors of the sun melding into each other, producing something soft and caressing like a feathery cloud. An atypical vanilla, non-sweet, non-foodie, though gourmand in structure, it emphasizes the woody, lightly spicy (cardamom, pepper) and musky-soft elements to project as a fluffy cashmere shawl on naked shoulders. borrowed

posts.title: Nostalgia is the kitschiest sentiment. Or is it?
posts.description: Young and older people alike love to reminiscence about things they loved in the turmoil of puberty or their formative years, from La Vie Est Belle by Lancôme to Tobacco Vanille Tom Ford via Coco Mademoiselle Chanel or Jungle Gardenia and White Shoulders; I suppose it gives us a sense of nostalgia, the strange excitement of reliving a period of our lives when we were not so sure of certain things
